title: Sanctification
definition: Sanctification is God’s work of making believers holy and conforming them more to the image of Christ.
summary: Sanctification is God’s work of making believers holy and conforming them more to the image of Christ.
christFocus: Jesus saves His people not only from guilt but also for holiness, and the Holy Spirit forms Christlike life within them.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Sanctification is the ongoing work of God in the believer after salvation. Those justified by faith are also being changed by grace, trained to turn from sin, and formed into the likeness of Christ.

This growth is not produced by human effort alone. Believers participate through obedience, repentance, prayer, Scripture, and fellowship, but the power belongs to the Holy Spirit who works within them.

Sanctification keeps grace from being misunderstood as permission to remain unchanged. Christ forgives sinners and then leads them into new life where holiness becomes the fruit of belonging to Him.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many believers become discouraged because they are not growing as quickly as they hoped. Sanctification gives patient hope: God is at work even through slow obedience, repeated repentance, and daily dependence on the Spirit.

This doctrine also corrects shame-based change. Christlike growth is not fueled by self-hatred but by grace, truth, and the Spirit’s transforming power.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Yield your growth to Christ one step at a time. Confess sin quickly, use Scripture faithfully, seek help humbly, and rely on the Holy Spirit to make obedience possible where willpower alone cannot change you.
